A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q-learning convergence work. The main text, equations, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v4's new experimental figures and Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results and proofs, including Appendices A-D. Tables 1-2 summarize prior theoretical analyses; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original simulations in the environment described as Baird's counterexample. Figures 1-2 show weight-norm trajectories from 10 independent runs.

M1.justification: The tabular and linear Q-learning updates, epsilon-softmax policies, and adaptive temperature in Equations 2-4 are retained. The newly tested target-network, projection, and regularization variants are comparators, not changes to the method being analyzed.

E1.justification: v4 introduces the first actual evaluation environment: a seven-state, two-action, zero-reward simulation described as Baird's counterexample, used in Section 6 and Appendix E. v1 discusses Q-learning theoretically without experimental task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E introduces an evaluated comparison set consisting of unmodified linear Q-learning and variants with a target network, weight projection, or ridge regularization. v1's literature tables do not constitute empirical evaluations of these comparators.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 1,500-step experiment monitoring squared weight norms, with constant learning rate 0.1, discount 0.99, and epsilon 0.1. Section 6 specifies kappa0=100, whereas Appendix E specifies kappa0=10 for its comparisons. These are new experimental settings; the theoretical diminishing-step-size assumption remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a focused analysis of whether three common stabilization modifications alter weight boundedness relative to the unmodified update. This provides a limited component comparison on one environment, without broader sensitivity or distribution-shift analyses.

E5.justification: v4 introduces repeated-run and uncertainty reporting: Figures 1-2 describe 10 independent runs, plot mean squared weight norms, and shade minimum-to-maximum ranges. v1 contains no corresponding empirical statistical reporting. These ranges are not confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Figure 1 newly reports decreasing, bounded squared weight norms for unmodified linear Q-learning. Figure 2 adds trajectories for all four variants, showing bounded weights throughout the displayed experiment and the lowest final norm for ridge regularization. These are new outcomes, not performance improvements over a matching v1 experiment.

T1.justification: The main assumptions and Theorems 1-3 are retained, but several derivations change. Appendix A adds an eigenvalue expression for beta; C.3 adds beta to the drift-bound constant C7; C.4 restores a missing factor of 2^epsilon_alpha and corrects an initial-time factor. C.4 and D.5 also expand initial-transient bounds and specify theorem constants.

C1.justification: Both versions claim L2 convergence rates for linear Q-learning to a bounded set and for tabular Q-learning to the optimum, supported by the same stochastic-approximation and pseudo-contraction contributions. Adding 'in L2' to the title clarifies the scope already stated in v1 rather than changing the core guarantee.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains why discontinuous epsilon-greedy policies invalidate the key Lipschitz argument and invokes computational hardness to motivate bounded-set guarantees. It also adds interpretations of the simulations as supporting stability and of the unmodified method as avoiding the comparison variants' additional overhead.

D1.justification: v4 adds brief experimental implementation details, including target-network updates every 10 steps, projection radius 10, ridge coefficient 0.01, and simulation hyperparameters. Reproduction remains incomplete because feature vectors and initialization are unspecified, and the main and appendix experiments report different kappa0 values without explaining the difference.

R1.justification: v4 adds Kane et al. (2023) for hardness positioning and Marbach and Tsitsiklis (2001) for ergodicity context, while making Meyn's prior boundedness result more prominent. Table 1 changes Meyn's behavior-policy classification from epsilon-greedy to epsilon-softmax. Most other citation changes update publication or author metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, behavior-policy explanation, and selected proof passages receive targeted revisions. An Experiments section and Appendix E are added, and the conclusion is renumbered. The existing narrative sequence and organization of the theoretical sections and Appendices A-D remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 introduces graphical presentations of original learning dynamics: Figure 1 displays the unmodified method's trajectory and run range, while Figure 2 compares four methods with uncertainty shading. v1 has no such plots. The retained literature tables also receive lighter rules and some row reordering.

improvement.justification: Localized proof corrections in Appendices C.3-C.4 and clearer attribution to Meyn improve the precision of the retained theoretical contribution. The new plots add illustration, but their evidential value is limited: constant step sizes and the stated all-to-state-7 dynamics do not satisfy the theorem's assumptions, and Section 6 and Appendix E report different kappa0 values without explanation. The gains therefore support a modest improvement, not substantially stronger validation.
